The `userId` looked up here is `ctx.actor.userId`, which `resolveAccessReach`'s only caller shape (`ctx.actor.kind !== "user"` short-circuits to wholeTenant first) can only ever be: every AccessContext with a `user` actor is built exclusively by `accessContextFromRequest()` (access-context.ts), which sets `userId` to `req.user.sub` — the JWT's own authenticated subject, never a client-supplied path/body parameter. `accessContextForJob()`, the only other AccessContext constructor in the codebase, builds a `system` actor and never reaches this branch at all. The call therefore always fetches the CALLER's OWN user row (to resolve THEIR OWN legacy-role fallback, D-08 of Phase 75b, identical to the already-established `resolveGrants()`/`userIdsHoldingPermission()` pattern this function's own comment cites) and returns nothing beyond a `role` enum used only to compute that same caller's reach — there is no other tenant's row ever read or exposed, so no `where.tenantId` filter is meaningful here, the same category as the pre-authentication self-identity lookups already exempted above (auth.ts) though this one runs post-authentication.
